title: Perfectness of $Rf_*\mathcal{G}$ and base change
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $f:X\to S$ a proper morphism of finite
presentation, and let $\mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation
and flat over $S$. Then $Rf_*\mathcal{G}$ is a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_S)$,
and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change: for every
morphism $g:T\to S$ the canonical map

$$
Lg^*(Rf_*\mathcal{G})\;\longrightarrow\;Rf_{T,*}\mathcal{G}_T
$$

is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{O}_T)$.
Here the canonical map is [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]: it is the map of [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] followed by derived direct image of the derived-to-ordinary module pullback comparison, constructed using the adjunction [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint].

proof.text: By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $f$ is separated and of finite type, hence quasi-compact. The finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent and flat over $S$ by hypothesis. Apply [lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module] to $f$ and $\mathcal G$: for every $g:T\to S$ it identifies the canonical map $Lg^*Rf_*\mathcal G\to Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T$ as an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 36.30.4, Tag 0B91, clause (2), base-change conclusion; properness gives the quasi-compact separated hypotheses

proof.text: Regard $\mathcal G$ as a complex concentrated in degree $0$ and take $E=\mathcal O_X$ in [lem-pc-proper-support-perfect-direct-image]. The structure sheaf is perfect: on each affine open it is a free module of rank one in degree $0$ [def-pc-perfect-complex]. The support of $\mathcal G$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed], because finite presentation implies finite type. Since $X\to S$ is proper, $X$ itself is a closed subset proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; its closed subset $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)$ is proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](2). All hypotheses of the cited tensor theorem now hold, and $E\otimes^L\mathcal G\cong\mathcal G$, since $E=\mathcal O_X$ is the tensor unit. Its conclusion gives the required perfectness of $Rf_*\mathcal G$ (and agrees with the base-change map of step 1). This is the specialization used in the proof of Stacks Tag 0B91, clause (2).

proof_origin.place: Lemma 36.30.4, Tag 0B91, proof of clause (2), applying Lemma 36.30.1, Tag 0A1H

blueprint_proof_text:
The base-change assertion is
[lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module]; proper morphisms are
quasi-compact and separated. If the base is locally Noetherian
and $f$ is projective, the perfectness assertion follows from
[lem-pc-projective-noetherian-rf-perfect].
For a general proper $f$ of finite presentation the perfectness
assertion is the recorded classical input: Derived Categories of Schemes,
Lemma 36.30.4 (Tag [0B91](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B91))
reads, in clause (2), ``Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f:X\to S$ be a
proper morphism of finite presentation. ... Let $\mathcal{G}$ be an
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite presentation, flat over $S$. Then
$Rf_*\mathcal{G}$ is a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O}_S)$ and its
formation commutes with arbitrary base change.'', which is this lemma;
its proof is the cohomology-and-base-change theorem of the same section
(Lemma 36.30.1, Tag [0A1H](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A1H)),
not decomposed here.

split_report.summary: The base-change map follows from the existing relatively flat base-change lemma. For perfectness, specialize the general tensor-and-proper-support theorem of Stacks Tag 0A1H, as the proof of Tag 0B91 does. That general theorem is a new unsplit node; its conclusion is substantially broader than this item. Mathlib has no matching direct-image theorem.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes the base-change sentence of the blueprint proof via lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module. Step 2 realizes its general perfectness sentence by the explicit E=O_X and degree-zero G specialization of Tag 0A1H, as in the proof of Tag 0B91.
